A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GradMem work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original KV-retrieval, bAbI, Short SQuAD, and WikiText-103 results, alongside memory-writing analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, memory ablations, larger-model latency measurements, and PG19 text-reconstruction experiments.

M1.justification: The core reconstruction-based WRITE updates and second-order meta-training remain unchanged. Appendix I adds an adaptation using learned LoRA adapters during WRITE with a frozen, adapter-free READ model. Appendix J also tests directly optimized per-layer KV memory as an alternative parameterization.

E1.justification: The original KV-retrieval, bAbI QA1–QA5, Short SQuAD, and WikiText-103 tasks are retained. Appendix I adds PG19 text reconstruction from compressed memory, a limited additional dataset and task beyond the previous continuation and question-answering evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated TTT-Linear and LaCT comparators on the existing KV-retrieval task in Table 8. Figure 8 additionally compares latency against TTT-Linear, TTT-MLP, and LaCT. These substantially extend comparison with competing test-time-training methods; the original baseline set is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols sweep memory size and WRITE steps, vary Mamba state configurations, and compare input-level versus per-layer memory under matched and enlarged budgets. Added latency tests use larger models, 4k–16k contexts, and batch size 1. PG19 evaluation introduces reconstruction-capacity thresholds over 8–64-token sequences. These extend evaluation design rather than establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained WRITE-step extrapolation, meta-learning ablation, and reconstruction-loss analyses, v2 adds memory-size sensitivity tests in Appendix F, constrained-state Mamba comparisons in G, and memory-placement ablations in J. Appendix D extends latency scaling analyses. These directly probe memory bottlenecks, parameter efficiency, and compute amortization.

E5.justification: The existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over three runs is retained. Table 8 additionally reports LaCT's best of three runs alongside its mean and standard deviation because of high variability. This changes the reported summary practice without establishing increased run counts for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1's scores are unchanged, while Table 2 fills the previously missing higher-K GradMem language-modeling result with 2.91±0.01 cross-entropy. Tables 7–9 and Figures 8, 10, and 11 add substantial comparison, capacity, latency, and ablation results. For example, Table 9 reports 99% reconstruction accuracy through 32 tokens with Llama-3.2-3B, K=2, and one memory vector. Appendix D's new latency prose conflicts with Figure 8, limiting exact timing interpretation.

T1.justification: The formal setup, objectives, update equations, and computational break-even derivation in Equations 1–11 are retained. Algorithm 1 restates the existing procedure. Correcting Figure 2's WRITE-loop label from outer to inner clarifies terminology already correctly explained in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: few-step gradient-based memory writing, advantages over forward-only writing at fixed memory size, capacity scaling, and transfer to natural-language tasks. Added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 corrects the earlier Short SQuAD K=1 superiority claim and qualifies larger-K gains as task-dependent, including no bAbI improvement. The retained SQuAD scores are 38.1 for K=1 versus RMT's 42.6, with 54.9 at larger K. New appendices explain memory bottlenecks, qualify input-memory advantages when per-layer capacity increases, and acknowledge unequal comparator state sizes and coarse reconstruction-capacity estimates.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds detailed per-model settings and total memory-state sizes in Table 6, clarifies WRITE-head initialization and curriculum stabilization, and specifies previously unspecified larger-K settings. Appendix K supplies Algorithm 1 and minimal PyTorch-like code. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the repository was already linked in v1.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds LaCT/TTT Done Right and Nested Learning references and expands the existing TTT discussion with Table 4's comparison against Titans, Atlas, and LaCT. This sharpens distinctions in memory level, update granularity, and objectives while retaining the original research positioning. Other bibliography changes largely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose are preserved. v2 makes targeted language corrections, clarifies memory initialization and second-order ablation terminology, updates author/publication information, and adds an impact statement, acknowledgements, and appendix contents guide. The added scientific sections do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 6–9, latency Figure 8, memory-analysis Figures 10–11, and Algorithm 1 with code Figure 12. Existing displays remain, including v1 Figure 8 as v2 Figure 9. Figure 3 moves, Figure 6 is reflowed, and captions are refined, producing a substantial expansion of visual and technical presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through previously missing TTT comparisons and controlled memory-budget and placement analyses, while expanded settings and pseudocode improve reproducibility. Section 3.5 also corrects interpretations inconsistent with Table 2. Larger-model accuracy evidence remains limited to short reconstruction, and Appendix D's 8B latency prose conflicts with Figure 8: 1870 ms versus roughly 700 ms at 4k for one WRITE plus READ. This reporting flaw limits the efficiency evidence but does not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative validation and clarity.
